To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the dynamic metal-organic-framework system 1 exhibits reversible single-crystal to single-crystal transformations and combines distinct donor and receptor characteristics.

a dynamic MOF with a soft core (flexible) and rigid side arms (rigid) exhibits a reversible, single-crystal-to single-crystal transformation upon exposure to PdCl2 in CHCl3, with the metal ions incorporated within the flexible polyether core.

1) a new MOF has been prepared that exhibits dramatic reversible single-crystal to single-crystal transformations; 2) the MOF exhibits both donor and acceptor properties, allowing for the uptake of Pd(II) ionic species; and 3) the MOF is able to detect H2 S in aqueous solution, a process that is accompanied by a colorimetric response.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and synthesis of new metal-organic frameworks and the investigation of their structure-property relationships.
the design of a new class of dynamic MOF systems, with a flexible soft core and rigid peripheral arms.
the synthesis of a novel amphoteric metal–organic framework (MOFs), which combines distinct donor and receptor characteristics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the combination of a rigid core and a flexible side arm can lead to a dynamic MOF system that can exhibit both donor and acceptor properties.
the combination of a flexible core and rigid side groups can lead to dynamic MOFs with interesting properties.
the combination of a soft core and flexible arms in a single system provides an effective strategy for designing dynamic MOFs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have designed a molecule L with rigid sidearms (arylalkynylethynyl) to calibrate the dynamic motion of the flexible polyethers in the core and have demonstrated that the resulting MOF, [Pb2 (L)2 (H2 O)2 ]·2 CH3 OH·H2 O (1) exhibits reversible single crystal to single crystal transformations.

the amphoteric character of the MOF allows the system to be both a soft and hard material, and that the dynamic nature of the system allows the soft and hard character to be interchanged in a reversible manner.

we have designed a molecule that is capable of both accepting and donating, a rare feat in supramolecular chemistry, and we have used the molecule as a building block to create a material that exhibits a rare combination of structural dynamics and functional characteristics.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a rigid side arm design can be used to control the mobility of the core and that the resulting amphoteric system can be used as a molecular platform for the selective uptake of metal ions and the sensing of small molecules.
a flexible core and rigid side-arms can be an advantageous combination for the design of dynamic MOFs.
the use of rigid side arms in a dynamic system can provide an effective way to control molecular mobility, which in turn can lead to new and interesting properties.
